boundary_rationale: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6, tier: byte, 'who is this coming up from the wilderness') opens the mi-zot ascending-question formula (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier: Song.3.6 and Song.8.5), beginning an unattributed third-person description of Solomon's escorted carriage that continues without a gender-marked speaker change through the palanquin's construction (web:Song.3.9-Song.3.10) to its close: צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte, 'go out and see, daughters of Zion'), an imperative call to a vocative distinct from the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair used elsewhere (sweep: 1 verse for the daughters-of-Zion form).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A cut at the 3:10|3:11 seam, where צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte, 'go out and see, daughters of Zion') opens on the book's one daughters-of-Zion vocative, was weighed and rejected: the referential chain closing the prior verse in תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.10, tier: byte) and the שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה/שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה recurrence (oshb:Song.3.9, oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte) run past the imperative rather than break at it, so the verse reads as this unit's own close, corroborated at tier-3 by the setumah standing at Song.3.11 itself rather than at the 3:10 joint (single-witness only).
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Deviation disclosure: the bulk of this unit (Song.3.6-Song.3.10) is third-person processional description rather than direct address; the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, so lyric_address is used here as the closest-fit default rather than a literal address-form match throughout. The WLC marks setumah breaks at Song.3.5 (front-seam), Song.3.8, and Song.3.11 (all single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only) -- the layer tracks this processional unit's internal joints without arguing any of them.

boundary_rationale: The seam verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) opens a new exchange against its own front seam: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first-person singular — לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) — while oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with the repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (byte tier) 'return, return, the Shulammite; return, return', addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית, byte tier: 1 verse / 1 token book-wide; its bet-prefixed counterpart בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית later in the same verse is a distinct byte-tier string, itself 1 verse / 1 token; together, at the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton, the pair sweeps to 1 verse / 2 token occurrences), an addressee-and-person shift of tier-1 class. The catchword נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after bracket this single-verse span on both seams (skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide). Within the verse the summons is followed by מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) 'why do you gaze at the Shulammite' — WEB “Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?” (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1). Whether the second half is spoken by the same voice as the opening summons is argued from the bytes alone (not from the WEB [SPEAKER] heading), so the call-and-question is held as one exchange rather than split at an unmarked internal line.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row forward into web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2's wasf opening was rejected: the imperative summons and its dance-of-Mahanaim question form a closed rhetorical unit distinct in form from the body-part praise that begins the next verse.

wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The dance-of-Mahanaim construal at this WEB 6:13 seam verse is held open, not decided. The voice assignment of the mah-tehezu clause is held open between the plural cohortative וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a 1cp form with a 2fs suffix, and the 2mp prefix-conjugation form תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) in the same clause — evidence weighed on both sides of the plural-speakers-and-feminine-addressee question without deciding it. The row sits inside the offset zone (MT 7:1 = WEB 6:13), and its structured refs carry the mandated dual-cite qualifier.

boundary_rationale: The brothers' deliberation opens with a 1cp possessive, אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) 'a little sister [belongs] to us', marking a new speaker-group distinct from the woman's own 1cs voice throughout the surrounding movements (this achot token is role-split from the bride-epithet achoti used earlier in the book) — the sister here is theirs, not his address to her; the speaker-group identification itself is a content inference rather than a named form, though the keeper-and-vineyard chain at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same 'my mother's sons' phrase, links the same group across the book. WEB: “We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister...” (web:Song.8.8). The wall/door conditional in 8:9 continues the same 1cp voice — נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) — as a compact, self-contained mashal, and the immediately preceding verse (web:Song.8.7) closes under a setumah division. The row's own back seam carries a byte-true straddling device: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) is answered clause-for-clause by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) — the wall-noun pair is the plene singular spelling's only two sites in the book (skeleton tier: 2 verses, MT 8:9 and MT 8:10), byte tier at each ref, identical only once cantillation is stripped (accent_stripped tier as a pair); the same lexeme's defective-spelled plural שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת (oshb:Song.5.7, byte tier) stands as a third lexeme site the plene sweep does not reach. The seam nonetheless survives the straddle because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at the oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 boundary is itself in-verse and marked, not because the wall-and-breast answer is absent.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the span to Song.8.8-Song.8.10 as a dialogue_exchange (the brothers' deliberation answered by her wall-and-breasts retort) was considered, but the two verses here are voiced by one speaker-group without an answering party, so this row is held as a self-contained deliberative epigram_unit and the exchange is left to resolve at the next seam.
